clue.text: American chose to cook eastern dish

indicators.note: to cook is to work raw ingredients into something new, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An American decides to make an Eastern dish for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cook' rearranges AMERICAN CHOSE into MACARONICHEES; the abbreviation E for 'eastern' finishes it. 'Eastern dish' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'dish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta baked in a cheese sauce is a familiar comfort-food dish.

clue.text: Funny group, Karl and The Monks

parts.note: Karl Marx, the philosopher behind communism
monks are members of a religious order, addressed as brothers

explanation.surface: A comic troupe made up of a man called Karl and a band named The Monks.
explanation.walkthrough: Groucho, Harpo, Chico and co. share a surname with Karl the economist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood comedy family troupe is the classic example of a funny group of performers.

clue.text: Bird often seen on building site

definitions.meaning: the tall lifting machine towering over construction work

explanation.surface: A bird spotted around a construction site.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a long-necked wading bird and a lifting machine, the machine named after the bird's shape.

clue.text: Slackening corps' objective

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a mission is a goal or objective

explanation.surface: An army unit's aim is to ease off.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A remission is an easing or abatement, as when a disease's symptoms lessen.

clue.text: Almost nobody died? Yes, twelve

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: no one means nobody
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
aye (here AY) is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: A question about whether almost nobody died, answered that twelve did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts NONE to NOON; AY is the archaic spelling of aye, yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock in the daytime is midday, the middle of the day.

clue.text: One with claws caught her slip, perhaps

parts.note: a cat is an animal with claws
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A clawed creature tripped a woman up.
explanation.walkthrough: A slip is a cricket fielding position behind the batter, there to take catches; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip fielder in cricket is one example of a player whose job is to take catches.

clue.text: Rugby game doesn't start at these odds

indicators.note: a word that doesn't start has lost its opening letter

parts.note: sevens is rugby played with seven players a side

explanation.surface: A rugby match fails to kick off, as the bookmakers had predicted.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby sevens is a short, fast form of the game played seven a side.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds of one to one, where a winning bet doubles the stake, are called this in betting.

clue.text: One eating fish given charge for cutlery?

indicators.note: given here means the cutlery word is handed the charge word to follow it

parts.note: a spoon is an item of cutlery
a bill is a charge to be paid

explanation.surface: A diner tucking into fish gets billed for the cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: This wading bird with a flat broad beak feeds on fish and other small water creatures.

clue.text: Proper mess in front field

parts.note: proper, genuine, means real

indicators.note: only the front of the word mess is taken, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A real muddle at the front of a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a field or sphere of activity, as in the realm of science.

clue.text: How kangaroo may be caught unawares?

definitions.text: How kangaroo may be caught unawares?

parts.words: How kangaroo may be caught unawares?
parts.note: a kangaroo is caught mid-leap, and the idiom for being caught off guard uses the same words

explanation.surface: Wondering how to take a kangaroo by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being caught unprepared literally describes a kangaroo in mid-bound.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means taken by surprise, unprepared, while a hopping animal is literally in mid-jump.

clue.text: Good sitting posture for part of course

definitions.meaning: sitting with the spine held upright
the straight stretch of a racecourse or track opposite the finishing one

explanation.surface: Advice that good posture is part of a training course.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright spine is good posture, and the straight on the far side of a racetrack has the same name.

clue.text: Lucky to be not so much asleep?

indicators.note: to be in that state places the word for not so much within the word for asleep

parts.note: asleep means a-bed, in bed
less means not so much

explanation.surface: Considering yourself fortunate to sleep less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'asleep' is 'in bed', so the clue really says LESS is in BED; 'Lucky' is the definition, not the surface sense of luck in sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Blessed can mean fortunate or favoured, as in being blessed with good health.

clue.text: Party-giver shortly meets reflective girl, glory be!

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: the host gives the party

indicators.note: a reflective name looks the same in a mirror, reading identically backwards

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A party host briefly meets a thoughtful girl, to cries of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims HOST to HOS; ANNA reads the same both ways, hence 'reflective'.
explanation.definitionFit: This shout of praise to God, used in hymns and worship, works like an exclamation of glory.

clue.text: Wardrobe likely to conceal daggers

indicators.note: the words wardrobe likely conceal the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A wardrobe is a likely place to hide knives.
explanation.walkthrough: These daggers are typographical marks, the dagger symbol used for footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, the dagger symbol used for footnotes is an obelus, and these are its plural form.

clue.text: Transport: repeat run when ordered

indicators.note: ordered here means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for a transport service: run the route again when told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' is a verb here, to delight, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to carry them away with delight, to fill them with rapture.

clue.text: Criterion for replacing dirty cask

indicators.note: replacing means putting the letters back in different places

explanation.surface: A standard for swapping a dirty barrel for a clean one.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard of measurement or comparison used to judge things.

clue.text: Material for carving kinky teaspoons

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: Odd-shaped teaspoons serve as stuff to whittle.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft talc-rich rock is easily carved into ornaments and figures.

clue.text: Unsympathetic, like a rhino?

definitions.meaning: a rhinoceros's horny snout, read literally

explanation.surface: Asking whether an uncaring person resembles a rhinoceros.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for tough and unsentimental describes, read literally, an animal with a horned, tough snout.

clue.text: St Wenceslas's feast day?

parts.note: the carol Good King Wenceslas has the king look out on the feast of a different saint, so the feast day in that song is this one

explanation.surface: A question about when Saint Wenceslas is celebrated.
explanation.walkthrough: The carol says 'Good King Wenceslas looked out on the feast of' another saint, celebrated on 26 December.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's opening line sets the scene on the feast of the first Christian martyr, Boxing Day.

clue.text: A month, helpers said, appearing as a very long time

definitions.note: plural noun used as a singular idea, as in 'for decades'

parts.note: Dec is the short form of December

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: aides are helpers or assistants

explanation.surface: Helpers claim a single month feels like an age.
explanation.definitionFit: Spans of ten years each, used loosely to mean ages, as in 'I haven't seen him for decades'.

clue.text: Share out much broadcasting

indicators.note: broadcasting means spoken over the air, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: a lot means much

explanation.surface: Plenty of programmes are shared out on the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or apportion shares among people.

clue.text: Supersede corded cloth with fine fabric

parts.note: rep is a fabric with a ribbed or corded surface
lace is a fine openwork fabric

explanation.surface: Swapping a ribbed material for a delicate one.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede something is to take its place, to stand in for it.

clue.text: Kingsley & Son put together wrongly

parts.note: Kingsley Amis, the English novelist

explanation.surface: A literary father and son assembled badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingsley Amis's son Martin is also a novelist, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone awry has gone wrong; the adverbial use 'take it amiss' means wrongly.

clue.text: Money being short, settled down with a sweet

indicators.note: being short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: cash is money
sat means settled down, took a seat

explanation.surface: Short of money, someone sits down with a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassata is an Italian dessert of layered ice cream with candied fruit.

clue.text: Sort of acid, could I be? Wrong

parts.note: the question could I be? is answered as am I?
no, as a reply, says you are wrong

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they could be acidic and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a two-line exchange: 'Am I?' 'No.'
explanation.definitionFit: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins, so the word names one sort of acid.

clue.text: Sanctioned, having peddled drugs round province

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to push drugs is to peddle them
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called the Province

explanation.surface: Penalised for dealing drugs around a region.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is known in the UK simply as 'the Province'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctioned in its penalising sense means punished, penalised for an offence.

clue.text: Due to be in old part of mansion

parts.note: a wing is a part of a large house

explanation.surface: Someone is expected in an old section of a country house.
explanation.definitionFit: Money still owed is outstanding, payable; both words mean yet to be paid.

clue.text: Pastoral events demanding reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are given a new shape

explanation.surface: Country happenings calling for change.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the 1381 English uprising, and 'reform' also rearranges PASTORAL EVENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1381 uprising of English rural workers demanding an end to serfdom fits rustic events calling for change.
